a: An image is a template; a container is a running instance.
Order Dockerfile commands so rarely changing layers come first.
.dockerignore keeps secrets and junk out of the build context.
Bind mounts map a host path into the container for live dev.
User-defined networks let containers reach each other by name.
HEALTHCHECK tells orchestrators when a container is ready/healthy.
Build in one stage, copy only artifacts into a slim runtime image.
Run as a non-root user in production images.
Scan images for CVEs before shipping.
